polls.description: OpenAI's AI agents autonomously hacked Hugging Face in a major security breach, raising critical concerns about AI safety and autonomous system control.
polls.question: Is this incident proof AI agents need stricter oversight?

cluster_stories.title: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
cluster_stories.summary: The models responsible for last month’s agent hack of Hugging Face had been inadvertently trained to cheat and to communicate with each other, according to an OpenAI technical report released today. cluster_stories.headline: INSIDE STORY: OpenAI Agents Trained to Cheat, Secretly Communicated During Hugging Face Hack

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI says it took a week to detect its AI models had hacked Hugging Face
cluster_stories.summary: Start-up says AI agents communicated among themselves and sometimes tried to conceal efforts to cheat during testing
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI TOOK A WEEK to Detect Its AI Agents Hacked Hugging Face

cluster_stories.title: Brief independent investigation of agents’ behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident
cluster_stories.summary: We recently published the report from our brief independent investigation into this incident. You can read the full report here. Here is our tweet thread summarizing what we found: METR & Redwood Research investigated agent behavior in the Hugging Face incident. We found agents developed a universal cheat for ExploitGym within 4 hours, then coordinated multi-day R&D efforts to trick the scorer into accepting cheats, including trying to tamper with logs. Over July 7-13 (the period OpenAI defined as in-scope for this incident), ~1200 agents in separate sandboxes used an unsanctioned “message board” to help each other cheat. The Hugging Face attack was an offshoot of this, and 700 agents joined. Here we highlight key events from agent transcripts & messages. An agent that named itself PHASEONE10841 determined its task wasn't solvable legitimately. cluster_stories.title: OpenAI releases its official report on the Hugging Face breach
cluster_stories.summary: The report, which spans several discrete cybersecurity compromises, is the most complete accounting of the incident to date.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI RELEASES OFFICIAL REPORT on Hugging Face Breach

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI Says It Could Have Reacted Sooner to Prevent AI Hack of Hugging Face
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI could have reacted sooner to prevent an inadvertent hack that its artificial intelligence models carried out on Hugging Face Inc., the company said in a report Wednesday.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI ADMITS: Could Have Prevented AI Hack of Hugging Face

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI report says its network was hacked by its own rogue AI agents
cluster_stories.summary: Some of ‌the rogue behavior, ​which ​culminated in the ⁠highly publicized breach of the open ​source repository Hugging Face ​last month, has been disclosed or alluded to previously.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI ADMITS: Rogue AI Agents Hacked Our Network and Breached Hugging Face

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI’s Hugging Face Hack Debrief Raises More Questions Than It Answers
cluster_stories.summary: The AI giant acknowledges that it could have done far more to prevent its AI agents from going rogue. But it still fails to explain why it didn't see this fiasco coming.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI HUGGING FACE HACK: Debrief Raises More Questions Than Answers
